question.text: Mr. Aakash Verma, Fund Manager of Indus Cat III AIF — a long-only fund investing 100% in large-cap listed Indian equities (blue-chip focus) — must state the benchmark in the PPM. The fund does NOT use leverage and does NOT take short positions. Which benchmark is MOST appropriate per Example 10.7 of Chapter 10?

answer.text: NIFTY 50 TRI or S&P BSE SENSEX TRI — broad-based large-cap free-float market-cap-weighted indices; Total Return variant chosen so dividend accrual is captured in the comparison.
A fixed 10% p.a. hurdle rate, since all Cat III AIFs must use absolute-return benchmarking.
NIFTY Small Cap 100, because the fund is a Category III AIF and Cat III always benchmarks to small-caps.
CRISIL Composite Bond Index, because Cat III AIFs must always use a debt benchmark to reflect capital preservation.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Example 10.7, for a large-cap long-only listed-equity fund the appropriate benchmarks include NIFTY 50 or S&P BSE Sensex. Section 10.5.6 / GIPS guidance supports using the Total Return Index variant so that dividend accrual is captured in the comparison. The Trap: Option B misapplies an absolute-return benchmark, which is not the workbook prescription for a long-only listed-equity strategy. Options C and D attach the wrong asset class entirely (small-cap and debt respectively). Note: Always select the Total Return Index (TRI) variant over a price index when the fund reports NAVs inclusive of dividends, so the comparison is on a like-for-like total-return basis.
